Ayrıca: {source:7:2} indirilen kitaptan dolayı elçinin göğsünde bir darlık olmaması; {source:18:6} {source:26:3} {source:35:8} inanmayanlar yüzünden elçinin kendini tüketmemesi; {source:18:57} {source:32:22} hatırlatıldıktan sonra yüz çevirenin en büyük haksızlığı yapması; {source:72:17} Rabbinin zikrinden yüz çevirenin yüklendiği azap; {source:43:36} Rahman'ın zikrine gözünü kapatana bir şeytanın yoldaş kılınması; {source:92:14} {source:92:15} {source:92:16} ateşe yalnızca en bedbahtın girmesi ve onun yalanlayıp yüz çeviren diye tarif edilmesi; {source:88:23} {source:88:24} yüz çevirip inkâr edeni hatırlatıcının değil Allah'ın cezalandırması; {source:80:7} arınmamanın sorumluluğunun elçide olmaması; {source:43:41} {source:43:42} elçi görse de görmese de sonucun Allah'ın elinde olması

## Fayda: zararın karşıtı, iyiliğe taşıyan



نفع kökü kendi başına bir yön taşır. Araplar faydayı önce zararın karşıtı olarak tanımlardı: {ar:النفع ضد الضر, tr:en-nef'u diddu'd-darr, gloss:fayda zararın zıddıdır, source:"ن ف ع,B001"}. Sonra da bir araç olarak: {ar:ما يستعان به في الوصول إلى الخيرات, tr:mâ yusteânu bihî fi'l-vusûli ile'l-hayrât, gloss:iyiliklere ulaşmak için yardım alınan şey, source:"ن ف ع,B001"}. Bu tanıma göre fayda bir varış yeri değil, oraya götüren şeydir. Hatırlatmanın faydası da kendisinde değil, götürdüğü yerdedir. Surede o yer on dördüncü ayetteki kurtuluşa ermek ve on beşinci ayetteki anmak ve namaz kılmaktır. Türkçeye geçen "menfaat" kelimesi kişisel çıkara kaymıştır. "Menfaatçi" bir kınama sözüdür. Arapçadaki fayda ise yüzünü başkasına döner. Araplar {ar:رجل نفاع إذا كان ينفع الناس ولا يضرهم, tr:raculun neffâun iẕâ kâne yenfau'n-nâse ve lâ yedurruhum, gloss:insanlara fayda verip zarar vermeyen kişiye neffâ' denir, source:"ن ف ع,B001"} derlerdi.

<!-- v16:augment brief=augment9 model=opus para=12 kind=refs -->
Ayrıca: {source:2:219} aynı şeyde faydanın ve büyük günahın bir arada bulunup birbiriyle tartılması

Fayda ve zarar ikilisi, son ayette sayfaları anılan İbrahim'in kavmine yaptığı hatırlatmanın ölçüsüdür. Allah elçisine İbrahim'in haberini okumasını söyler. İbrahim babasına ve kavmine neye taptıklarını sorar. Putlara taptıklarını ve onların başından ayrılmadıklarını söylerler. İbrahim sorar: {ar:قَالَ هَلْ يَسْمَعُونَكُمْ إِذْ تَدْعُونَ, tr:kâle hel yesmeûnekum iẕ ted'ûn, gloss:dua ettiğinizde sizi duyuyorlar mı, source:26:72}, {ar:أَوْ يَنفَعُونَكُمْ أَوْ يَضُرُّونَ, tr:ev yenfeûnekum ev yedurrûn, gloss:yoksa size fayda ya da zarar mı veriyorlar, source:26:73}. Kavmi buna bir cevap veremez, yalnızca babalarını böyle bulduklarını söyler. İbrahim de Âlemlerin Rabbini anlatır: {ar:ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَنِى فَهُوَ يَهْدِينِ, tr:elleẕî halakanî fe-huve yehdîn, gloss:beni yaratan ve bana yol gösteren O'dur, source:26:78}. Bu, surenin ikinci ve üçüncü ayetlerinin söylediğidir. Sözünü de faydanın son sınırıyla bitirir: {ar:يَوْمَ لَا يَنفَعُ مَالٌۭ وَلَا بَنُونَ, tr:yevme lâ yenfeu mâlun ve lâ benûn, gloss:ne malın ne oğulların fayda vereceği gün, source:26:88}, {ar:إِلَّا مَنْ أَتَى ٱللَّهَ بِقَلْبٍۢ سَلِيمٍۢ, tr:illâ men etallâhe bi-kalbin selîm, gloss:ancak Allah'a temiz bir kalple gelen müstesna, source:26:89}. Başka bir anlatımda İbrahim putları kırdıktan sonra aynı soruyu sorar: {ar:أَفَتَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا يَنفَعُكُمْ شَيْـًۭٔا وَلَا يَضُرُّكُمْ, tr:e-fe-ta'budûne min dûnillâhi mâ lâ yenfeukum şey'en ve lâ yedurrukum, gloss:Allah'ı bırakıp size hiçbir fayda da zarar da veremeyen şeylere mi tapıyorsunuz, source:21:66}. Mal ve oğullar on altıncı ayette tercih edilen dünya hayatının malıdır. İbrahim'in hatırlatması, insanın bel bağladığı şeylerin ölçüldüğü bir faydanın hatırlatmasıdır. Bizim ayetteki şart da bu ölçüyü taşır.

<!-- v16:augment brief=augment9 model=opus para=13 kind=refs -->
Ayrıca: {source:26:79} yediren ve içiren Rab: İbrahim'in sözünün surede otlağı çıkarana kadar uzanması; {source:21:64} {source:21:65} kavmin bir an kendine dönüp putların konuşmadığını kabul etmesi, sonra yeniden tersine dönmesi: İbrahim'in sorusunun hemen öncesi; {source:5:76} {source:6:71} {source:10:106} {source:13:16} {source:20:89} {source:22:12} fayda da zarar da veremeyene tapmanın sorgulanması: İbrahim'in ölçüsünün başka yerlerdeki tekrarı; {source:60:3} kıyamet günü akrabanın ve evladın fayda vermemesi; {source:63:9} malın ve evladın Allah'ı anmaktan alıkoymaması uyarısı; {source:2:123} {source:20:109} {source:74:48} o gün şefaatin fayda vermemesi; {source:6:158} vakti geçince imanın fayda vermemesi; {source:40:52} o gün zalimlere mazeretlerinin fayda vermemesi; {source:43:39} o gün azapta ortak olmanın bile fayda vermemesi; {source:10:98} imanı kendisine fayda veren tek kasaba: vaktinde gelen imanın faydası

Kur'an faydanın ne olduğunu bir sel sahnesinde de söyler. Gökten su iner, vadiler kendi ölçülerince akar, sel üstünde kabarık bir köpük taşır. Ziynet ya da eşya yapmak için ateşte eritilen madenin de benzer bir köpüğü olur. Sonra ayrım gelir: {ar:فَأَمَّا ٱلزَّبَدُ فَيَذْهَبُ جُفَآءًۭ ۖ وَأَمَّا مَا يَنفَعُ ٱلنَّاسَ فَيَمْكُثُ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ, tr:fe-emme'z-zebedu fe-yeẕhebu cufâen ve emmâ mâ yenfau'n-nâse fe-yemkuŝu fi'l-ard, gloss:köpük atılıp gider; insanlara fayda veren ise yerde kalır, source:13:17}. Burada fayda, kalan şeyin adıdır. Bu sahne, beşinci ayetteki selin sürüklediği çerçöple ve on yedinci ayetteki "daha kalıcı" ile birlikte surenin büyük sel manzarasını kurar. Dokuzuncu ayetin bu manzaraya kattığı şey şudur: hatırlatmanın faydası, akıp gittikten sonra geride kalan sudur.

<!-- v16:augment brief=augment9 model=opus para=14 kind=refs -->
Ayrıca: {source:13:18} sel misalinin hemen ardından Rabbine icabet edenlerle etmeyenlerin ayrılması; {source:14:24} {source:14:25} {source:14:26} kökü sağlam ağaç ile yerin üstünden koparılıp karar bulamayan ağaç: kalanla gidenin bir başka misali; {source:23:41} zalim bir kavmin selin sürüklediği çerçöpe çevrilmesi: beşinci ayetteki kelimenin insanlar için kullanılması

## Kırbanın yanı ve değnek

Bu kök iki somut eşyaya da ad vermiştir. Bu adlar ayetteki "fayda vermek" anlamının yerine geçmez. Onun yanında duyulur ve faydanın nasıl bir şey olduğunu elle tutulur kılar.

İlki deri bir su kabının parçasıdır. Mezâde yolda su taşımak için kullanılan büyük bir deri kaptır. Bu kabın iki yanındaki deri yarılır ve her yana bir parça yerleştirilir. Araplar bu parçaya nuf'a derlerdi: {ar:النُّفعة في جانبي المزادة يشق الأديم فيجعل في كل جانب نفعة, tr:en-nuf'atu fî cânibeyi'l-mezâde yuşakku'l-edîmu fe-yuc'alu fî kulli cânibin nuf'a, gloss:nuf'a, su kabının iki yanında deri yarılarak her yana konan parçadır, source:"ن ف ع,B002"}. Bu söz parçanın kabın duvarına yerleştirildiğinden başka bir şey söylemez. Ama bu kadarı da yeter: parça artık kabın kendi duvarıdır ve kabın yanlarını suyu tutacak biçimde tamamlar. "Fayda" kelimesinin kökü, suyu tutan bir kabın parçasına ad olmuştur. Sel sahnesinde fayda yerde kalan suydu. Burada da suyu tutan derinin bir parçasıdır. Hatırlatma ile ilgili kök de zaten tutmakla başlıyordu: zikir bir şeyi korumak, aklında tutmaktır. Hatırlatma, ancak tutulduğu bir kaba yerleşirse fayda verir. Kendisine okutulanı tutan elçi, başkalarında da bu tutmayı arar. Ailesinin resmini bütünleyen başka kökler de vardır. İkinci ayetteki "yarattı" fiili deriyi kesmeden önce ölçmeyi, birinci ayetteki "Rab" deriyi yağla terbiye etmeyi, yedinci ayetteki "açık" tulumu çalkalamayı, on birinci ayetteki "uzak durmak" ise kabın iki yanını adlandırır. Böylece surenin kelimeleri tek bir tulumda buluşur. Bu son kelimenin yanında bir ses yankısı da duyulur: fayda veren parça kabın yanına yerleştirilir, en bedbaht ise hatırlatmayı kendi yanında, uzakta tutar. Bu bir dil yankısıdır, ayetin kendi sözü değildir.

<!-- v16:augment brief=augment9 model=opus para=16 kind=prose ref=69:12 -->
Hâkka suresinde hatırlatmanın onu tutan bir şeye yerleşmesi açıkça söylenir, hem de yine suyla birlikte. Su taştığında insanların akıp giden gemide taşındığı anlatılır ({source:69:11}). Sonra bunun amacı söylenir: {ar:لِنَجْعَلَهَا لَكُمْ تَذْكِرَةًۭ وَتَعِيَهَآ أُذُنٌۭ وَٰعِيَةٌۭ, tr:li-nec'alehâ lekum teẕkiraten ve teiyehâ uẕunun vâiya, gloss:onu sizin için bir hatırlatma kılalım ve onu tutan bir kulak tutsun diye, source:69:12}. "Tutmak" diye çevrilen fiilin kökü, Yûsuf suresinde yüklerin konduğu kapların adıdır: kardeşlerin {ar:أَوْعِيَتِهِمْ, tr:ev'iyetihim, gloss:onların yük kapları, source:12:76} ve kardeşinin {ar:وِعَآءِ, tr:viâ', gloss:kap, source:12:76}. Kulağın hatırlatmayı tutması, kabın içindekini tutmasıyla aynı kökten söylenir.

<!-- v16:augment brief=augment9 model=opus para=16 kind=refs -->
Ayrıca: {source:62:5} Tevrat yüklenip de onu taşımayanlar: üstte taşınan ile içte tutulan arasındaki fark

İkinci eşya değnektir. Araplar değneğe nef'a da derlerdi ve bu adın faydadan türediğini söylerlerdi: {ar:النَّفعة العصا وهي فعلة من النفع, tr:en-nef'atu'l-asâ ve hiye fa'letun mine'n-nef', gloss:nef'a değnektir, adı faydadan gelir, source:"ن ف ع,B003"}. Değnek elde taşınır, yolda ona dayanılır, onunla hayvan sürülür. Fayda burada elden bırakılmayan ve yürürken iş gören bir şeydir. Kur'an değneğin bu işlerini, son ayette sayfaları anılan Musa'nın ağzından sayar. Kelime aynı değildir ama eşya aynıdır. Allah Musa'ya sağ elinde ne olduğunu sorar. Musa şöyle cevap verir: {ar:قَالَ هِىَ عَصَاىَ أَتَوَكَّؤُا۟ عَلَيْهَا وَأَهُشُّ بِهَا عَلَىٰ غَنَمِى وَلِىَ فِيهَا مَـَٔارِبُ أُخْرَىٰ, tr:kâle hiye asâye etevekkeu aleyhâ ve ehuşşu bihâ alâ ğanemî ve liye fîhâ meâribu uhrâ, gloss:bu benim değneğimdir; ona dayanırım, onunla koyunlarıma yaprak silkelerim, onda başka işlerim de var, source:20:18}. Ardından Allah ona değneği atmasını söyler ve değnek koşan bir yılana dönüşür. Sonra şöyle der: {ar:قَالَ خُذْهَا وَلَا تَخَفْ ۖ سَنُعِيدُهَا سِيرَتَهَا ٱلْأُولَىٰ, tr:kâle huẕhâ ve lâ tehaf se-nuîduhâ sîratehe'l-ûlâ, gloss:al onu, korkma; onu ilk hâline döndüreceğiz, source:20:21}. Musa'nın gündelik işler için kullandığı değnek bir anda bir ayete, bir işarete dönüşür, sonra yine eski hâline döner. Dokuzuncu ayetin "fayda"sı bu sırayı izler. Yolda dayanılan bir şey, aynı zamanda Rabbi gösteren bir işaret olabilir. Değnek surede bir başka kelimenin ailesinde de görünür. Üçüncü ayetteki "yol gösterdi" fiilinin ailesinde değnek, taşıyanın önünden gittiği için hâdî adını alır. İki kök aynı eşyayı ayrı yüzlerinden adlandırır: biri önden gidişinden, öbürü dayanılmasından.

Ayrıca: {source:20:22} {source:20:23} değnekten sonra elin "bir başka ayet" diye anılması: değneğin de bir ayet olduğunu söyler; {source:2:60} {source:26:63} Musa'nın değneğiyle taşa ve denize vurması: gündelik değneğin ayete dönüşmesi

strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Exod.20.8	ذ ك ر (B004/B009); Hebrew זכור, Sabbath memory	The Hebrew imperative zakhor, cognate with the commentary's ذ ك ر, makes remembering the Sabbath an act of sanctification; it gives a Torah precedent for remembrance becoming enacted worship.
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Exod.13.9	ذ ك ر (B003/B004); Hebrew זכרון, law in the mouth	Passover is to be a sign and zikkaron so that the Lord's law will be in Israel's mouth, closely joining visible memorial, oral retention, and practice in the manner developed by the commentary.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Exod.24.12	written tablets given for instruction	God gives Moses tablets, law, and commandment written for Israel's instruction, a direct antecedent for the commentary's link between received revelation, written pages, and later teaching.
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Num.10.10	ذ ك ر (B004/B009); Hebrew זכרון, trumpet memorial	Trumpet blasts over offerings become a memorial before God; this is a precise ritual and auditory counterpart to the commentary's broad sense of dhikr as worshipful remembrance rather than bare recollection.
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Deut.5.15	ذ ك ر (B003); remembering deliverance through Sabbath practice	Israel is to remember slavery and redemption and therefore keep Sabbath; the verse makes memory of an earlier act the reason for present obedience, as the commentary makes recovered memory lead to prayer and action.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Deut.6.6	words placed upon the heart	The words commanded by God are to be upon the heart, furnishing an especially close Hebrew Bible counterpart to the commentary's image of a reminder being held inwardly rather than merely heard.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Deut.6.7	repeat the words to children in daily speech	The heart-held words are to be repeated to children at home and on the way, an exact domestic form of the commentary's movement from retained revelation to another person's remembrance.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Deut.6.12	warning not to forget the liberating Lord	Deuteronomy warns Israel not to forget the Lord after entering prosperity; it supplies the ethical danger against which the commentary defines reminder as the opposite of letting something escape the mind.
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Deut.8.18	ذ ك ر (B003/B001); remember God who gives power for wealth	Israel must remember the Lord who gives power to acquire wealth, a cognate-root use that places remembrance beside material benefit and corrects self-sufficient possession in a way relevant to the commentary's test of what truly benefits.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Deut.32.46	set hearts on the testimony and command children	Moses tells Israel to set its heart on the testimony and command its children to do it, giving a close parallel to the commentary's sequence of inward retention, teaching, and ethical effect.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Deut.32.47	word is life, not an empty matter	The testimony is not an empty word but Israel's life and the source of long days; this directly supplies a biblical measure of the beneficial word that the commentary seeks in ن ف ع (B001).
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Josh.1.8	book in the mouth, meditation, doing, success	Joshua keeps the Torah book in his mouth and meditates on it continually so as to do it and prosper, closely linking page, recitation, retained thought, action, and beneficial outcome.
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Ps.20.8	ذ ك ر (B004/B007); remembering God's name against worldly power	Against reliance on chariots and horses, the psalmist remembers the name of the Lord; it illuminates the commentary's dhikr as both naming God and a counterweight to reliance on worldly means.
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Ps.111.4	ذ ك ر (B003); wondrous works made memorable	The Lord makes his wonders into a zekher, a memorial; this cognate-root formulation closely supports the commentary's claim that visible divine acts in the world are material for reminder.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.119.93	never forget precepts that give life	The psalmist will not forget God's precepts because through them God gives life, directly binding anti-forgetfulness to benefit in the way the commentary's conditional reminder does.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.3.1	do not forget teaching; heart keeps commandments	Proverbs pairs not forgetting instruction with the heart's keeping commandments, a compact wisdom analogue to the commentary's mental preservation of reminder before outward obedience.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.7.3	teaching written on the tablet of the heart	Instruction is bound on the fingers and written on the tablet of the heart, joining physical inscription with interior retention and sharpening the commentary's pages-and-container imagery.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.22.18	words kept within and ready on the lips	Wise words are pleasant when kept within and ready on the lips, a direct parallel to the commentary's claim that what is held mentally can become the hearer's own spoken word.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.30.8	message written on tablet and book for future days	A prophetic charge is fixed on tablet and book for the time to come, offering a precise counterpart to the commentary's concern with preserving a word on pages for readers beyond its first hearing.
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Isa.46.8	ذ ك ر (B003); remember and stand firm	Isaiah calls transgressors to remember and stand firm; this cognate-root imperative supplies a Hebrew prophetic form of the commentary's tadhkirah addressed to those in danger of turning aside.
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Isa.46.9	ذ ك ر (B003/B006); remember former things and confess one God	The command to remember former things leads to the confession that God alone is God, directly linking the commentary's prior-word remembrance with its insistence on the creator over powerless objects.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.51.2	look to Abraham as ancestral point of instruction	Isaiah directs its hearers to look to Abraham and Sarah as the beginning of a blessed people; it gives a biblical way of making Abraham a remembered source for later communal instruction beside the commentary's Abrahamic sheets.
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Isa.57.11	ذ ك ر (B003); fear, not remembering, and not laying to heart	Isaiah asks whom Israel feared so that it neither remembered God nor laid him to heart, a striking inverse of the commentary's pairing of reverent fear with remembrance held inwardly.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Jer.2.32	people forget God for days without number	Jeremiah contrasts a bride who remembers clothing with a people that have forgotten God, providing a vivid prophetic parallel to the commentary's account of forgetfulness as abandonment of the very one to be remembered.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Jer.31.33	Torah written within and on hearts	Jeremiah relocates Torah from external writing to the inward heart; this complements and complicates the commentary's relation between earlier sheets and the listener's internal capacity to hold the reminder.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ezek.3.21	righteous person warned, takes warning, and lives	When the righteous person receives warning and does not sin, that person lives and the prophet is delivered; this necessary positive counterpart to the watchman scene maps the commentary's reminder when it actually benefits its hearer.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ezek.33.32	hear prophetic speech but do not do it	Ezekiel's audience listens to the prophet's pleasant song but refuses to do what it says; this gives a concrete biblical instance of hearing without the inward holding and action that the commentary calls beneficial.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Hos.4.6	forgotten Torah followed by reciprocal forgetting	Hosea says that because the people forgot God's Torah, God will forget their children; it makes the commentary's memory-forgetting contrast into a judicial outcome.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Mal.2.7	priestly lips guard knowledge; people seek Torah from the mouth	Knowledge is guarded by the priest's lips and sought by the people from that messenger's mouth, a close counterpart to the commentary's teacher who receives and explains a prior word to others.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Neh.8.8	public Torah reading with explanation for understanding	The Torah is read aloud, explained, and made understood; this exact public-reading scene supplies a Hebrew Bible analogue to the commentary's recitation followed by clarification for its listeners.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ezra.7.10	study, do, and teach Torah	Ezra sets his heart to study Torah, do it, and teach its statutes; this is a particularly clear threefold pattern for the commentary's received word, personal retention, and subsequent reminder.
strong	tevrat	paralel	WLC:Jonah.3.5	city believes warning and changes its practice	Nineveh believes God's warning, fasts, and changes response; the scene shows the conditional benefit of a prophetic reminder becoming visible in a hearer's conduct.
strong	tevrat	motif	Wisdom of Solomon 13:1	creation's visible goods should disclose their maker	Wisdom faults people who see the good things of creation yet fail to know their maker, a Jewish-Hellenistic counterpart to the commentary's created order as a public reminder that can still be missed.
strong	tevrat	motif	Wisdom of Solomon 13:10	human-made objects called gods	Wisdom calls those unhappy who place hope in dead, human-made things named gods; it tightly parallels the commentary's Abrahamic examination of whether cult objects can truly help their worshippers.
medium	tevrat	yorum_gelenegi	Mishnah Avot 1:1	Moses receives Torah and transmits it through generations	Avot's chain from Moses to Joshua, elders, prophets, and the Great Assembly gives a Jewish traditional model for revelation preserved through successive human reminders.
medium	tevrat	yorum_gelenegi	Mishnah Avot 5:6	Moses' staff among twilight-created marvels	By treating Moses' staff as one of the exceptional creations at twilight, Avot recasts the commentary's ordinary, useful staff as a primordial sign; the contrast is itself an instructive later reception of the object.
strong	tevrat	motif	1 Maccabees 2:51	remember ancestral deeds for honor and lasting name	Mattathias tells his sons to remember the ancestors' deeds so as to receive honor and an everlasting name, directly connecting remembered prior tradition with the commentary's secondary sense of dhikr as renown.
medium	tevrat	motif	Baruch 3:9	commandments of life and learned wisdom	Baruch calls Israel to hear commandments of life and learn wisdom, a Jewish scriptural articulation of remembered instruction as life-giving benefit rather than mere information.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.2.1	pay attention to heard things lest they drift away	Hebrews urges greater attention to what was heard so that it does not drift away, an exceptionally close New Testament formulation of the commentary's concern with a received word being lost unless held.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Jas.1.24	hearer immediately forgets after looking	James depicts the hearer who looks and then immediately forgets; this supplies the concrete negative image behind the commentary's contrast between reminder retained and reminder that passes by.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1John.2.24	let what was heard from the beginning abide	The community is told to let the original message abide in it; this directly joins the commentary's prior word to an enduring inner dwelling rather than a momentary hearing.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Luke.2.19	sayings treasured and pondered in the heart	Mary keeps and ponders the sayings in her heart, a narrative counterpart to the commentary's image of an inward vessel that holds what has been spoken.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Luke.11.28	hear God's word and keep it	Jesus calls blessed those who hear God's word and keep it, a concise Christian parallel to the commentary's distinction between an offered reminder and beneficial, obedient retention.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:John.2.22	disciples remember a saying and believe Scripture	After the resurrection the disciples remember Jesus' saying and believe both Scripture and his word, showing remembrance as a later recovery that makes prior speech intelligible.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Acts.8.35	reading Scripture followed by explained proclamation	Philip begins from the passage being read and explains its good news, closely matching the commentary's pattern of a received written word being made intelligible to another person.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Acts.20.31	unceasing personal admonition to remember	Paul tells the elders to remember his three years of unceasing warning; it gives a concrete apostolic example of reminder as sustained pastoral responsibility rather than coercive control.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Acts.20.32	word of grace builds and gives inheritance	Paul entrusts hearers to the word able to build them up and give an inheritance, an explicit account of a proclaimed word's beneficial result.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.10.11	former events written as instruction for later readers	Israel's earlier events happened as examples and were written for instruction at the end of the ages, a close Christian parallel to the commentary's former pages and visible history functioning as reminder.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.15.4	former writings give instruction, endurance, and hope	Paul says everything written beforehand was written for instruction so that readers may have hope, directly supporting the commentary's claim that previous scripture remains a usable word for later hearers.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.12.5	forgotten exhortation addressed to children	Hebrews reproves readers for forgetting the exhortation that addresses them as children, making a prior scriptural warning itself the object that must be recalled.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Luke.8.14	word choked by cares, riches, and pleasures	In the thorny soil the heard word is choked by cares, riches, and pleasures and reaches no maturity; this directly supplies a Christian picture of why benefit may fail where the commentary contrasts lasting good with worldly preference.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.1.21	creation known but not honored or thanked	Although people knew God, they neither honored nor thanked him and became futile in thought; this is the negative continuation of creation as a reminder that the commentary says can be seen yet not retained.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Pet.3.5	deliberate overlooking of creation and water	The opponents deliberately overlook the creation of earth through and by water through God's word, a striking Christian counterpart to the commentary's water-and-creation reminders that can be ignored.
strong	incil	paralel	SBLGNT:Heb.11.7	Noah warned of unseen things, reverent, building an ark	Noah acts in reverent fear after a warning about unseen things and prepares an ark; it joins the commentary's fearful receiver, warning, and flood-water scene in one Christian retelling.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.7.24	heard words put into practice on rock	The wise builder hears Jesus' words and does them, building on rock; this provides a vivid Christian counterpart to the commentary's demand that retained reminder issue in stable, beneficial action.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.4.17	Timothy sent to remind communities of apostolic ways	Timothy is sent to remind the Corinthians of Paul's ways as taught everywhere, an unusually exact New Testament instance of a messenger being delegated to perform remembrance for others.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Phil.4.9	learned, received, heard, seen, then practiced	The Philippians are to practice what they learned, received, heard, and saw; its ordered reception-to-practice sequence closely reflects the commentary's account of reminder becoming the hearer's own deed.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Tim.3.15	sacred writings able to make wise for salvation	Sacred writings are able to make Timothy wise for salvation, a direct Christian analogue to the commentary's prior sheets as a word whose benefit lies in the good to which it leads.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.10.3	annual sacrificial remembrance of sins	The sacrifices contain an annual remembrance of sins, a distinct Christian liturgical use of memory that bears on the commentary's discussion of dhikr's ritual as well as mental forms.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.15.8	honor with lips while heart remains distant	Jesus contrasts lip-honor with a heart far from God; this sharpens the commentary's warning that spoken remembrance is only a later branch if the inward holding of the word is absent.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.6.7	land drinks rain and yields crop, receiving blessing	Land that drinks repeated rain and bears a useful crop receives blessing; it gives a Christian agrarian analogue to the commentary's water, pasture, and beneficial remainder imagery.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.6.8	thorns after rain are rejected and burned	Land yielding thorns after the same rain is rejected and ends in burning, a specific contrary image for the commentary's one reminder producing different outcomes in its hearers.
medium	incil	yorum_gelenegi	Didache 4:1	remember the one who speaks God's word and honor that speaker	The Didache tells its hearer to remember day and night the person who speaks God's word and to honor that person; it is an early Christian reception of the teacher-reminder relation developed in the commentary.
